clue.text: How to prepare course work

parts.note: read as a description of a written work explaining how to make the courses of a meal, with 'course work' posing as schoolwork

explanation.surface: A student asks how to get coursework ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course work' looks like school assignments, but the course is a dish at dinner and the work is a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A volume of recipes is literally a written work telling you how to prepare each course of a meal.

clue.text: Took a picture partially displayed by browser

indicators.note: partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone photographed a creature that was partly visible while it grazed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Browser' looks like web software, but it is an animal that browses on leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a forest animal that feeds by browsing on leaves.

clue.text: Sort of drama all that's missing from large collection?

definitions.meaning: a style of gritty realist domestic play

definitions.text: all that's missing from large collection?
definitions.meaning: from the saying everything but the ___, used of a huge assortment

explanation.definitionFit: A domestic realist play is named after the sink, and the saying 'everything but the ___' names the sole item left out.

clue.text: Half revoke Papal order, displaying gall

indicators.note: order means putting the letters into a new arrangement
half points to one half of the word, here its back three letters

explanation.surface: A pope reverses half an edict, showing nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gall' looks like cheek, but it is a growth on a plant; 'Half' takes OKE from revoke.
explanation.definitionFit: An oak apple is a round growth, a gall, formed on oak trees by wasp larvae.

clue.text: Lunch packed with punch?

parts.note: read as a packed lunch that is really a blow to the mouth, the 'filling' being a fist

explanation.surface: A packed lunch comes with a fruit punch.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a punch in the mouth, pictured as a meal of knuckles.

clue.text: Most reserved box I got for hour after one

indicators.note: after puts the box behind the one

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: got for means the letter I is swapped in for the letter standing for hour

explanation.surface: Someone describes the shyest person with a box obtained one hour later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I got for hour' replaces the H in CHEST with I, giving CIEST, and 'after' puts that behind the I from 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Icy describes a cold, distant manner, so the iciest person is the most reserved.

clue.text: Sustains ruling people can keep dog

indicators.note: keep means hold, so these letters enclose the next piece

parts.note: the ins are those in power

explanation.surface: The authorities may allow a dog to be kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sustains' means suffers, as in sustaining a loss.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain a loss or injury is to incur it.

clue.text: Ignoring Liberal characteristic of President

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out the next item

parts.note: like means characteristic of, typical of

explanation.surface: A President's trait is to ignore Liberal concerns.
explanation.definitionFit: Ike was the nickname of US President Dwight Eisenhower.

clue.text: Drink that's twist with nip added

parts.note: to snake is to twist and wind

explanation.surface: A drink with a twist and a nip added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twist' and 'nip' sound like cocktail garnish and a measure, but they give SNAKE and BITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Snakebite is a British drink of lager mixed with cider.

clue.text: Composer seen in book and craft fair

explanation.surface: A composer turns up in a book and at a craft fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft fair' reads as one event, but craft gives ART and fair gives OK separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Béla Bartók was a Hungarian composer of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Spotted short Frenchman touring South America

indicators.note: touring means going round, so these letters enclose the next piece
short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for monsieur, a Frenchman

explanation.surface: A short Frenchman was seen travelling around South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South America' reads as one place, but South gives S and America is the definition; 'short' cuts UNCLEAN to UNCLEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Sam is the personification of the United States, a nickname for America.

clue.text: Guru's disciple to hunt for audience

indicators.note: for audience means the word is as heard by listeners, a sound-alike

explanation.surface: A guru's follower goes out to hunt for an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Audience' looks like a crowd to be hunted for, but it signals a sound-alike of SEEK.
explanation.definitionFit: Sikhism takes its name from the Punjabi for a disciple or learner of the Gurus.

clue.text: Keep A CD for playing that's unreadable

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A CD is held back for playing, its contents a mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadpan expression gives nothing away, so the face cannot be read.

clue.text: Single subject within a book's covers an item of contention

indicators.note: within puts these letters inside the next piece
covers means the outside letters of the word

explanation.surface: A single subject inside a book's covers proves a point of dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covers' takes the first and last letters of book, B and K, which go around ONETOPIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Having this with someone means having a grievance to argue over.

clue.text: Yarn in French that horror film (all but) pinches

indicators.note: pinches means grips, so these letters hold the next piece
all but means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a chiller is a frightening film
en is the French word for in

explanation.surface: A tale in French that a horror film steals from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' looks like a story, but it is a soft tufted thread; 'all but' cuts CHILLER to CHILLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Chenille is a velvety tufted yarn used in embroidery and soft furnishings.

clue.text: One might succeed with a real burst

indicators.note: burst suggests the letters fly apart and reform

explanation.surface: Someone could prosper with a genuine sudden effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeed' looks like do well, but it means inherit.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal heir is someone who may succeed to, or inherit, an estate.

clue.text: Old linesman from FA introducing short film

indicators.note: introducing puts this piece before the next one

parts.note: FA stands for Fanny Adams, as in sweet FA, meaning nothing, the letter O

explanation.surface: An elderly line judge from the Football Association introduces a brief film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'FA' looks like the Football Association, but 'sweet FA' is British slang for nothing; the linesman is a writer of lines of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid was a Roman poet, an ancient writer of lines of verse.

clue.text: King with triumphant expression crushes resistance in Afghan town

indicators.note: crushes means sits on top of, which in a down clue puts this piece above the next

parts.note: aha is a cry of triumph
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A king's victory cry crushes the resistance in an Afghan town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crushes' is positional: in a down entry AHA sits on R, coming before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Kandahar is a major city in southern Afghanistan.

clue.text: I and mine return home to Delaware, perhaps

indicators.note: return means the pieces are read back to front

explanation.surface: Someone and their family go back to their home in Delaware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delaware' looks like the US state, but it is a Native American people.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipi is a conical tent dwelling used by Native American peoples such as the Delaware.

clue.text: Weak and ultimately vile brew stirred

indicators.note: brew suggests the letters are mixed up together
ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A feeble, nasty-tasting brew is stirred.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirred in the sense of roused from sleep or inactivity.

clue.text: Skip verse that actor's mad about

indicators.note: about means round, so these letters enclose the next piece
mad suggests letters going wild and rearranging

parts.note: the actor's name taken as its own letters

explanation.surface: An actor is crazy about leaving out a verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' shuffles ACTOR into CAORT, and 'about' puts V inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip about playfully is to frolic or prance.

clue.text: Some tennis shots are not straight

definitions.text: Some tennis shots are not straight

parts.words: Some tennis shots are not straight
parts.note: read as a description of strokes played with the back of the hand foremost, which also suggests indirect, sly remarks

explanation.surface: Some tennis strokes go crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: A compliment that is indirect or ambiguous is called this, after the tennis stroke.

clue.text: For my sake stopped regularly in Russian city

indicators.note: stopped regularly means letters are halted at regular intervals, keeping every other one

explanation.surface: Someone pleads to stop regularly for their sake in a Russian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stopped regularly' takes the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of FORMYSAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Omsk is a large city in southwestern Siberia, Russia.

clue.text: It takes pluck, one going into lead

indicators.note: going into places this letter inside the next word

parts.note: the star is the lead performer
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Courage is needed for one person to take the lead role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pluck' looks like courage, but it means plucking strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitar is an Indian stringed instrument that is plucked.

clue.text: Happy couple from Rome clutching old cut flowers

indicators.note: clutching means holding, so these letters go round the next piece

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals

indicators.note: cut means the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A happy couple from Rome hold an old bunch of cut flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut flowers' reads as a bouquet, but 'cut' trims OLD to OL.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladioli are tall plants grown for their spikes of colourful blooms.

clue.text: Understand criticism

definitions.meaning: a cutting remark aimed at someone

explanation.definitionFit: Slang 'dig' means appreciate or get; a dig is also a sly jibe.

clue.text: Good guy in house is providing lifts

indicators.note: in places this piece inside the next

parts.note: ST, for saint, is a crossword good guy

explanation.surface: A kindly man in the house is giving people rides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Providing lifts' suggests giving rides, but it is the verb raising things up.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist something is to raise it up, so one that hoists is providing lifts.

clue.text: 7 heading for desert isle

indicators.note: heading for means the front letter of the following word

parts.note: the Isle of Wight lies off England's south coast

explanation.surface: A man heads out for a desert island.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is IKE, President Eisenhower, whose first name this is.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwight was the first name of US President Eisenhower, nicknamed Ike.

clue.text: Tea, not cold, a drink one's finishing off oneself

indicators.note: not means the following letter is left out

parts.note: char is British slang for tea
kir is a drink of white wine and blackcurrant
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone takes tea without ice and a drink before ending it all.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritual suicide by disembowelment, a Japanese way of killing oneself.
